recorded_feedback.summary: Candidate 1 is ready for evaluation. It has not been run or checked here. The signal solve solve(A, b) and the noise-covariance solve solve(A, N w_d) use the same untransposed signal matrix A, and neither depends on the other's result. This change does them as one multi-RHS solve(A, [b | N w_0..D-1]), controlled by a new trace-time constant, differometor.simulate.MERGE_SAME_MATRIX_SOLVES = True. It is in _solve_signal_and_noise. Setting the constant to False gives back the parent code path. The A^H noise-weight solve is unchanged, because sharing its LU failed the strict check before. Assembly-only k=1 frequency loop, all frequencies, design variables, topology, precision and the three JIT stages are unchanged. Notes are in experiments/notes/claude-structure-solve.md.
recorded_feedback.hypothesis: Doing both A-solves in one call guarantees a single LU(A) per frequency. That saves one n≈751 complex LU per frequency if XLA did not already merge the duplicate LU (not checked against HLO). It also replaces two custom_linear_solve and triangular-solve paths with one, in both the forward and reverse passes, so execution and compile time may drop. The gain is unmeasured and may be about zero if the LU was already merged. Numerically the factorization and pivots are the same. Only the multi-column triangular solves and the order in which A's cotangent terms are added change, at rounding level, much like frequency-batching candidate 7, which passed the strict check. The main risk is strict gradient index 161.

jobs.hypothesis: Target phases: forward compile (6.47 s) and gradient compile (1.29 s) in job 57ef1df7 (3b80507). Mechanism: the slot masks are per group, so if any single row reads an optimized index in a slot, every row's input in that slot carries a tangent. Examples are surface reflectivity and tuning on non-optimized mirrors, and space length on non-optimized spaces. Splitting off the all-constant rows and gradient-stopping all their slots removes their residuals and transposes. The forward computation is the same elementwise math on the same inputs, with an exactly remapped output selection. Prediction: forward and gradient compile decrease by about 0.1–0.5 s, depending on the share of constant rows, which is unknown. Execute is unchanged or slightly lower. Forward outputs should be bitwise identical, assuming XLA kernels are per-element identical across batch sizes (unverified; strict rtol covers it). The gradient should be identical or within reordering. Reject on a strict failure or a total slower than 19.57 s beyond noise.

Only simulate.py changed; setting ROW_SPLIT_PRUNING=False restores 3b80507.

Target phase: build, 0.807 s (3.7% of the first run) in full job f60d64b6 for 745f5c3.

The signal update instructions overwrite them in both sidebands, so ulp-level differences between NumPy and XLA never reach a solve.

jobs.hypothesis: Target phases: forward compile (6.47 s) and gradient compile (1.29 s) in job 57ef1df7 (3b80507). Mechanism: the slot masks are per group, so if any single row reads an optimized index in a slot, every row's input in that slot carries a tangent. The forward computation is the same elementwise math on the same inputs, with an exactly remapped output selection. Prediction: forward and gradient compile decrease by about 0.1–0.5 s, depending on the share of constant rows, which is unknown. Execute is unchanged or slightly lower. Forward outputs should be bitwise identical, assuming XLA kernels are per-element identical across batch sizes (unverified; strict rtol covers it). The gradient should be identical or within reordering. Reject on a strict failure or a total slower than 19.57 s beyond noise.

jobs.hypothesis:
Target phase: forward execute, 8.609 s (38.5% of the 22.366 s first run), full job ab12c14c29354bad9aa6dc024c91f8e6 on seed 96474bd. Gradient execute (1.475 s) is a secondary target.

Mechanism: the parent's "broadcast" mode builds a (101,751,751) complex broadcast of the noise matrix, about 0.9 GB, for the batched einsum. It is probably kept as an AD residual, and its cotangent becomes a dense (101,751,751) outer-product reduction. Earlier, the single-run pair noise-reuse c1 (f3139c7) to c2 (e525ee5) removed that broadcast with a GEMM and measured −0.9 GB RSS, forward −0.35 s, gradient −0.22 s and total −0.76 s. That GEMM changed rounding (gradient margin 0.949). rowmap instead performs, for each row, the same (751x751)x(751xD) product as the batched dot, without the broadcast.

Prediction: lower peak RSS (up to about 0.9 GB) and slightly lower forward and gradient execute. The upper bound is about 0.76 s; that is an opportunity bound, not an expected result. Possible costs are loop overhead and slightly higher compile time.

recorded_feedback.hypothesis:
Target phase: forward execute, 8.609 s (38.5% of the 22.366 s first run), full job ab12c14c29354bad9aa6dc024c91f8e6 on seed 96474bd. Gradient execute (1.475 s) is a secondary target.

Mechanism: the parent's "broadcast" mode builds a (101,751,751) complex broadcast of the noise matrix, about 0.9 GB, for the batched einsum. It is probably kept as an AD residual, and its cotangent becomes a dense (101,751,751) outer-product reduction. Earlier, the single-run pair noise-reuse c1 (f3139c7) to c2 (e525ee5) removed that broadcast with a GEMM and measured −0.9 GB RSS, forward −0.35 s, gradient −0.22 s and total −0.76 s. That GEMM changed rounding (gradient margin 0.949). rowmap instead performs, for each row, the same (751x751)x(751xD) product as the batched dot, without the broadcast.

Prediction: lower peak RSS (up to about 0.9 GB) and slightly lower forward and gradient execute. The upper bound is about 0.76 s; that is an opportunity bound, not an expected result. Possible costs are loop overhead and slightly higher compile time.

Bitwise equality of the XLA reduction is not guaranteed.

The risk is that A's gradient now adds its contributions from the loop path and the batched solves in a different order, which could shift the gradient at rounding level and fail strict. data.hypothesis: The parent's k=1 assembly loop runs the noise components and a dense 751x751 noise scatter in each of its 101 iterations. When none of the noise inputs is a real changing index, every row's noise inputs are bitwise identical. Building the noise matrix once and broadcasting it should keep forward outputs bitwise identical. The expected gradient change is only the order of the reduction over the noise-matrix cotangent (mainly db/angle). The loop body becomes smaller. Expected first-run gain is small (under 1 s), not measured. Memory may not fall because the broadcast einsum operand may still be stored at full size for the gradient pass.
data.change_summary: Candidate 1 (variant A, guarded noise reuse) on parent d09dc1d. Not executed: this session cannot run code, so it has not been imported or traced. Changes, all in differometor/simulate.py: (1) run_build_step checks that the real carrier/signal changing indices (before the dummy fill) share no index with any noise input index, including padding and grouped indices. If none overlap, it adds the static key component_groups['noise_row_reuse'] = (). (2) When that key is present, NOISE_ROW_REUSE=True and the scope is not 'signal_noise', simulate builds the noise matrix once with an unbatched update(parameters[0], ...) and broadcasts it to all rows. The per-frequency assembly lax.map then builds only the signal matrix. Solves and the noise einsum/contraction are unchanged. (3) _assemble_signal_and_noise skips the noise update when noise_matrix is None. Every other case runs the unchanged per-row parent code. Notes file created.

data.hypothesis: The broadcast operand in candidate 1's batched einsum is probably stored as a (101,751,751) complex128 forward residual (about 0.9 GB) and run as 101 GEMVs. Contracting the single noise matrix with one unbatched einsum should remove that buffer and turn the 101 GEMVs into one GEMM. Expected effect is lower peak RSS and slightly less forward/reverse execute time, not measured. Forward noise and all gradient coordinates may differ by reassociation rounding, so the strict check could fail.
data.change_summary: Candidate 2 (variant B) builds on validated candidate 1 (f3139c7). Candidate 1 full run 5089ae06 passed official and strict: forward outputs bitwise identical to the parent, max normalized gradient error 1.6e-8, first run 23.320 s against the parent's 23.840 s (not a paired repeat, so the gain is unconfirmed), peak RSS 9.93 GB. Candidate 2 is not executed: this session cannot run code. New knob NOISE_REUSE_MODE in differometor/simulate.py: "shared" (default, variant B) or "broadcast" (exactly candidate 1). With "shared", the single (NN,NN) noise matrix built once outside the loop goes directly into _solve_signal_and_noise. There, a 2-D noise matrix selects jnp.einsum("ij,dbj->dbi", N, noise_weights) instead of broadcasting to (101,751,751) for the batched bij,bj einsum. The 'solve' scope always uses broadcast because its loop slices noise rows. Solves are unchanged. Notes updated with candidate 1 results and the draft knob handoff.

data.hypothesis: The forward pass factors A for the signal and covariance solves (XLA may CSE these) and separately factors A^H for the noise weights. Reusing A's LU with a conjugate-transpose triangular solve should remove at least one batched 751x751 complex LU of 101 rows. Expected effect is a forward execute time reduced by up to about a third of the LU work, not measured. The noise weights come from a different factorization, so the strict gradient check may fail.
data.change_summary: Candidate 3 (not executed; this session cannot run code): shared LU factorization on the noise path, on top of variant A. New knob NOISE_FACTOR_REUSE=True in differometor/simulate.py:_solve_signal_and_noise. One jax.lax.linalg.lu(stop_gradient(A)) per signal row is reused by three lax.custom_linear_solve calls: the signal solve (trans 0/1), the adjoint noise-weight solve A^H y = s (trans=2; its transpose solves conj(A) z = x as conj(lu_solve(conj x, 0))) and the covariance solve. This replaces the separate LU of the transposed-conjugated matrix. NOISE_REUSE_MODE is set back to "broadcast" (variant A) to isolate the effect from variant B's thin gradient margin. Candidate 2 (e525ee5) full run ab7f50a0 passed official and strict: 22.564 s first run, peak RSS 9.03 GB (candidate 1: 9.93 GB), but strict gradient max normalized error 0.949 of 1.0. Notes updated.

data.hypothesis: Candidate 3 showed that the replicated direct custom_linear_solve with an explicit LU reproduces jnp.linalg.solve bitwise (signal error 0.0), and that the forward pass ran separate A factorizations (about 4 s and 3.5 GB removed). Sharing A's LU between the signal and covariance solves only, with A^H factored separately as before, should keep every output and the gradient at candidate 1's strict margin. It should also remove one batched LU: an expected forward saving of about 2 s and a first run of roughly 21 s, not measured.
data.change_summary: Candidate 4 (not executed; this session cannot run code) repairs rejected candidate 3. Candidate 3 (bb9a183, full f62c5c80): official PASS, strict FAIL. Gradient indices 33/161/180 failed, max normalized error 14.7. First run 18.65 s, forward execute 5.17 s, peak RSS 6.37 GB. Signal was bitwise identical; the drift comes from solving A^H through A's LU. Candidate 4: NOISE_FACTOR_REUSE is now a string ("off" | "direct" | "all") and set to "direct". In differometor/simulate.py:_solve_signal_and_noise, one LU of A is shared by the signal and covariance custom_linear_solves. The noise weights go back to the original jnp.linalg.solve on the explicitly transposed-conjugated matrix (separate LU, as in the parent). NOISE_REUSE_MODE stays "broadcast" (variant A). Notes and knob handoff updated.

data.hypothesis: The signal/covariance LU sharing (bitwise-exact numerics) and the shared unbatched noise contraction (about −0.76 s, about −0.9 GB in candidate 2) act on separate parts of the computation, so the savings should add up to a first run of about 21.6 s. Not measured. The strict gradient margin is expected near candidate 2's 0.949, so a pass is plausible but not guaranteed.
data.change_summary: Final candidate 5 (not executed; this session cannot run code): candidate 4 plus variant B, i.e. NOISE_FACTOR_REUSE="direct" with NOISE_REUSE_MODE="shared" in differometor/simulate.py. Candidate 4 (96474bd, full ab12c14c) passed official and strict: first run 22.366 s, forward execute 8.609 s, gradient execute 1.475 s, peak RSS 8.13 GB. All forward outputs are bitwise identical to the parent and the max normalized gradient error is 6e-7. It is the best validated revision with a robust margin. Notes contain the full history (candidates 1–4 including the rejected candidate 3), the knob JSON handoff, remaining uncertainties and suggested next experiments.

data.hypothesis: Noise construction reuse (before the solves; bitwise forward) and merging the two A-untransposed solves into one multi-RHS solve (both strict-validated on their own) act on separate stages. The combination should pass strict with a large margin and run faster than f3139c7's 23.32 s. Additivity is not assumed; not measured.
data.change_summary: Candidate 6 (final; not executed): the coordinator's combination of parents f3139c7 (broadcast noise reuse) and 4c12600 (merged same-matrix multi-RHS solve). differometor/simulate.py settings: NOISE_REUSE_MODE="broadcast", NOISE_FACTOR_REUSE="off", and new MERGE_SAME_MATRIX_SOLVES=True. With the merge on, the signal RHS and the D noise-source RHS are solved by one jnp.linalg.solve on A. The A^H noise-weight solve keeps its separate factorization; the failed full LU reuse and the shared contraction are not used. Frequency chunk 1 with assembly-only scope, guards and fallback are unchanged. Candidate 5 (0550847, full cb43b777) passed official and strict: first run 21.649 s, forward execute 8.171 s, gradient execute 1.297 s, peak RSS 7.24 GB, gradient normalized error 0.949 (thin margin).

data.hypothesis: Doing both A-solves in one call guarantees a single LU(A) per frequency. That saves one n≈751 complex LU per frequency if XLA did not already merge the duplicate LU (not checked against HLO). It also replaces two custom_linear_solve and triangular-solve paths with one, in both the forward and reverse passes, so execution and compile time may drop. The gain is unmeasured and may be about zero if the LU was already merged. Numerically the factorization and pivots are the same. Only the multi-column triangular solves and the order in which A's cotangent terms are added change, at rounding level, much like frequency-batching candidate 7, which passed the strict check. The main risk is strict gradient index 161.
data.change_summary: Candidate 1 is ready for evaluation. It has not been run or checked here. The signal solve solve(A, b) and the noise-covariance solve solve(A, N w_d) use the same untransposed signal matrix A, and neither depends on the other's result. This change does them as one multi-RHS solve(A, [b | N w_0..D-1]), controlled by a new trace-time constant, differometor.simulate.MERGE_SAME_MATRIX_SOLVES = True. It is in _solve_signal_and_noise. Setting the constant to False gives back the parent code path. The A^H noise-weight solve is unchanged, because sharing its LU failed the strict check before. Assembly-only k=1 frequency loop, all frequencies, design variables, topology, precision and the three JIT stages are unchanged. Notes are in experiments/notes/claude-structure-solve.md.

data.hypothesis: Conjugating only the two fixed blocks by slice update gives the same values. The reverse pass only copies and conjugates, with no additions, so the gradient should match candidate 1 bit for bit. Inside the per-frequency assembly loop it avoids a whole-matrix conjugate-and-select and the mask construction, in both the forward and reverse passes. I expect a small saving of at most about 0.2 s, possibly within run-to-run noise. Nothing has been measured yet.
data.change_summary: Candidate 1 (4c12600) passed both the official check and the strict check in its full run: first run 22.495 s, against 23.840 s for the parent. Forward execution was 8.55 s and gradient execution 1.67 s; peak memory fell from 10.8 GB to 8.1 GB. All physical outputs matched the reference bit for bit. The largest normalized gradient error was 2.2e-6, with no failing entries. Candidate 2 adds an exact assembly change on top of candidate 1. The two fixed sideband blocks are now conjugated with slice updates, `SLICE_CONJUGATION = True` in `_assemble_signal_and_noise`, instead of a where-mask over the whole matrix. Setting the constant to False restores the old mask path. Notes now include candidate 1's runs and phase timings, and the operator proposals.

data.hypothesis: Candidate 3 should reproduce candidate 1: about 22.5 s first run and the same gradient (8.08e-10 maximum absolute error against the reference). That gives a second full sample of the best validated computation.
data.change_summary: Candidate 2 (39b23e3, slice-based conjugation) passed both the official and strict checks in its full run. Its gradient matched candidate 1 bit for bit, but it was slower: first run 22.794 s against 22.495 s. Reverse execution was about 0.2 s higher in every warm repeat. Candidate 3 sets SLICE_CONJUGATION = False, so the code that runs is candidate 1's again and the branch head sits on the best validated configuration. This is a repeat measurement of candidate 1, not a new idea. The notes record all run IDs, phase timings, the rejected idea and the final handoff with the operator JSON. The recommended operator is merge_same_matrix_solves with values {false, true}, from candidate 4c12600.

data.hypothesis: Slicing is exact. Both of A's cotangent contributions, from the merged solve and the A^H path, are still added at top level in the same order as before. The per-frequency pad and concatenation only touch disjoint entries, so the gradient should match candidate 1 bit for bit. If XLA had not already fused the work, the change removes one full-stack strided copy in the forward pass and one full-stack pad of the cotangent in the reverse pass. I expect a small saving of at most about 0.3 s, possibly none. Nothing has been measured yet.
data.change_summary: Candidate 3 (3e94580, candidate 1's code path again) passed both checks: first run 22.423 s, gradient identical to candidate 1. That gives two full samples of the merged-RHS computation, 22.495 s and 22.423 s, against the parent's single 23.840 s run. Candidate 4 follows the coordinator's lead and is untested. With the "assemble" scope, the loop body now splits each augmented signal block into its coefficient matrix and its RHS. The stacked coefficients (101, 751, 751) and RHS (101, 751) go straight to _solve_signal_and_noise through a new signal_rhs argument. This replaces a top-level slice of the 0.9 GB (101, 751, 752) stack. It is controlled by the trace-time constant SPLIT_SIGNAL_RHS = True; setting it to False restores the previous layout. Merged RHS and the mask conjugation path are kept, and topology, frequencies, variables and JIT stages are unchanged.

data.hypothesis: Combine guarded noise reuse and merged RHS solves with separately assembled coefficients and RHS.
data.change_summary: Port the reviewed split coefficient/RHS layout into the validated combination seed.

data.hypothesis: Parent 211f65a5f18d7b68deacc021e0d9eab874bd9df7, full job 6c6d3774738c4ed4b2bda1b9982c5072: forward execution took 8.571211 s, gradient compilation 5.024615 s and forward compilation 3.321781 s. data.hypothesis: Target phases: forward compile (6.47 s) and gradient compile (1.29 s) in job 57ef1df7 (3b80507). Mechanism: the slot masks are per group, so if any single row reads an optimized index in a slot, every row's input in that slot carries a tangent. Examples are surface reflectivity and tuning on non-optimized mirrors, and space length on non-optimized spaces. Splitting off the all-constant rows and gradient-stopping all their slots removes their residuals and transposes. The forward computation is the same elementwise math on the same inputs, with an exactly remapped output selection. Prediction: forward and gradient compile decrease by about 0.1–0.5 s, depending on the share of constant rows, which is unknown. Execute is unchanged or slightly lower. Forward outputs should be bitwise identical, assuming XLA kernels are per-element identical across batch sizes (unverified; strict rtol covers it). The gradient should be identical or within reordering. Reject on a strict failure or a total slower than 19.57 s beyond noise.
data.change_summary: Candidate 3 (3b80507, LOWER_SLOT_PRUNING) passed official and strict checks in full job 57ef1df7 and is kept as the new branch best. This is the lowest full-valid total observed in cohort 10567ad0 so far, but it is one observation and not yet confirmed. Candidate 4 adds row-level pruning. Each mixed component group is reordered on the host as [rows that read an optimized or linked index, all-constant rows], with parameter_indices and output_rows remapped to match. update() then evaluates the constant rows with every slot gradient-stopped, so they get no linearization. Only simulate.py changed; setting ROW_SPLIT_PRUNING=False restores 3b80507.

data.hypothesis: Target phases: forward compile (7.62 s) and gradient compile (1.96 s) in job 35abe628 (aa2b1ab). Candidate 1 (job 01ae3245) attributed about 2.9 s of that compile to the assembly linearization. Mechanism: the expanded parameter row carries a dense tangent, so the vjp forms derivative residuals and transposes for every component input. Many of those inputs never depend on a design variable; for example, 5 of the 7 surface inputs are constants. Gradient-stopping the slots that are provably constant gives them symbolic-zero tangents, so their residuals and transposes are never generated. Their true derivative is exactly zero, and stop_gradient is the identity in the forward pass. Prediction: forward and gradient compile both go down, and lower times go down slightly; the size is unknown and the ceiling is well under 2.9 s. Execute times stay the same or drop slightly. Forward outputs should be bitwise identical, and the gradient identical or within reordering (the dropped terms were exact 0*x contributions). Any forward difference or a strict failure rejects the candidate.

data.hypothesis:
Target phase: build, 0.807 s (3.7% of the first run) in full job f60d64b6 for 745f5c3.

Mechanism: build() runs about 30 eager jnp scalar ops per mirror or beamsplitter and several per space edge. Each one adds dispatch cost, primitive first-use compilation and host conversions (np.array of JAX scalars). NumPy gives the same structure without JAX dispatch.

Why outputs should stay bitwise identical: from the source, every such off-diagonal base entry is overwritten at the identical (row, column) by the carrier update instructions:
- mirror: rows [1,1,3,3], columns [0,2,0,2];
- beamsplitter: rows [1,1,3,3,5,5,7,7], columns [2,4,0,6,0,6,2,4];
- space: both directed entries.
The signal update instructions overwrite them in both sidebands, so ulp-level differences between NumPy and XLA never reach a solve.

Predicted: only the build phase drops. The ceiling is 0.81 s; the realistic saving is probably ≤0.3 s and unmeasured. Every other phase should be unchanged.

data.change_summary: Candidate 1 changes how the signal and noise solves step through the frequency axis. The loop (k=1) now covers only the signal solve, the explicit A^H, the noise-weight solve, the noise-source einsum, the covariance solve and the noise ASD. It steps through rows of the assembled matrices and the broadcast detector selections. Candidate 3 (47cd6495, k=2) passed the official check and failed strict. data.change_summary: Candidate 5 makes the operator's default the branch head. `FREQUENCY_CHUNK_SIZE = None` gives the full-vmap layout, and a new static `FREQUENCY_LOOP_SCOPE` keeps both tested loop layouts available: "signal_noise" (candidates 1–3) and "solve" (candidate 4). With None, assembly and solves run in one vmap with the same operations and order as the parent. The only differences are that the frequency-independent detector-selection preparation is computed once up front and the carrier connector gather happens before the broadcast multiply. Candidate 4 (3206ea9f, loop around solves only) passed the official check and failed strict. Its gradient was bit-identical to candidates 2 and 3. It also lost most of the gain: first run 23.546 s, forward 10.31 s, gradient 1.80 s, RSS 11.7 GB, warm median 12.21 s. So the strict drift comes from the solve and noise-contraction path whenever it runs inside a scan, regardless of chunk size or loop scope. Most of the reverse-pass and memory savings come from running assembly per frequency. Nothing was run locally.

data.hypothesis: Laser power affects the loop only through the carrier, which candidate 1 captured as a constant shared by all iterations. In the reverse pass, the scan added that constant's cotangents one frequency at a time across 101 iterations. The original vmap summed them in a single reduction, so the rounding differed slightly. Feeding the broadcast carrier entries and selections in as per-frequency inputs should restore the original order: per-frequency cotangents are stacked, summed by one reduction, then passed back through the gather. That should bring index 161 back within strict tolerance. Candidate 1's forward, gradient and memory gains should remain, apart from a few small extra broadcasts. Bitwise equality of the XLA reduction is not guaranteed.
data.change_summary: Candidate 2 keeps candidate 1's one-frequency-at-a-time loop (k=1) and changes how the frequency-shared inputs that depend on the parameters enter the loop. The gathered carrier connector entries and the detector carrier selections are now broadcast to all 101 rows before the loop and passed in as per-frequency inputs, instead of being captured as constants shared by every iteration. Candidate 1 (aa4d230f) passed the official check and failed strict. Its full run took 22.076 s versus 24.657 s for the parent. Forward execution took 9.12 s (parent 11.51), gradient execution 0.68 s (1.81), warm median 10.07 s (13.80), and peak RSS 7.27 GB (12.55). All physical outputs matched exactly. One gradient entry failed strict: index 161, boundary01.power, with relative error 1.9e-7 against rtol 1e-7. Nothing was run locally for candidate 2.

data.hypothesis: Candidates 1 and 2 match the forward outputs bit for bit, but their whole gradient differs from baseline at about 9e-10 relative L2, where the parent was at about 1e-17. So the difference comes from operations that only run in the reverse pass. My leading guess, unverified, is that with k=1 every inner batch dimension has size 1. XLA simplifies such dimensions away, which picks different dot and triangular-solve kernels for the reverse pass than the batched parent uses. With k=2 the batch dimension is real, which should bring back the parent's batched kernels and strict agreement on index 161. Blocks of two should keep most of the memory and cache benefit, at about 1% extra solve work from the padding. Expected: forward slightly above 9.0 s and RSS slightly above 7.3 GB.
data.change_summary: Candidate 3 changes one value from candidate 2: the frequency chunk size goes from 1 to 2. The loop now runs 51 blocks of two frequencies. Frequency 101 is duplicated once as padding and the duplicate is thrown away. Candidate 2 (aa7c3f93) passed the official check and failed strict, with the same failure as candidate 1. Its full run took 21.798 s (parent 24.657). Forward execution took 9.05 s, gradient execution 0.70 s, warm median 10.07 s, peak RSS 7.31 GB. All physical outputs matched exactly. Gradient index 161 (boundary01.power) failed with a value identical to candidate 1's to within about 1e-14. That rules out the carrier accumulation-order explanation.

data.hypothesis: Read from source: the baseline factors A^H separately from A in the forward stage (101 complex LUs at n=751, an estimated ~1e11 flops). It may also factor A twice unless XLA CSE merges the signal and covariance getrf calls. The JIT stages save the LUs as AD residuals. Reusing LU(A) for the A^H system (solve via U^H L^H P) should remove at least one LU batch from the forward stage. It should also remove the ~0.9 GB materialized A^H and one ~0.9 GB LU residual. Expected result: lower forward-stage and complete first-run time and lower peak memory. Gradient-stage cost and compile time should be about the same, and the outputs should differ only at rounding level (carrier and signal essentially identical).
data.change_summary: Candidate 1: share one LU factorization of each frequency's 751x751 signal matrix A. It now serves three solves: the signal solve, the noise-weight solve with A^H (previously a separately factored, materialized conjugate transpose) and the covariance solve. New helpers in differometor/simulate.py are lu_factor, _lu_solve (trans 0/1/2 via lax.linalg.triangular_solve) and solve_factored (lax.custom_linear_solve with matvec A x, or conj(A)^T x for the A^H case). The carrier solve and the public solve() are unchanged. The evidence and proposal are in experiments/notes/claude-linear-algebra.md.

data.hypothesis: After candidate 1 the forward pass (7.9 s warm) is dominated by one batch of 101 complex 751-LUs, about 4.5 s judging by candidate 1's saving. The block factorization needs about 1.1e8 complex FMA per frequency vs 2.8e8 for a dense LU. That should cut forward runtime by roughly 2–3 s, and the first run by a similar amount, while the gradient stage and compile time stay about the same. Because pivoting is now restricted to within blocks, numerical differences may be larger than candidate 1's. Carrier and powers should remain identical; signal, noise and gradient will differ at rounding level unless B1, B2 or S is ill-conditioned.
data.change_summary: Candidate 2 builds on candidate 1. It replaces the single dense 751×751 LU per frequency with a block/Schur factorization. The signal matrix's upper/lower sideband cross blocks are structural zeros per the source trace (build.py:177-266, 813-825, 1373-1374). So A = [[diag(B1,B2), Q],[R, M]] is factored as two 286×286 LUs, W = P⁻¹Q, and an LU of the 179×179 Schur complement S = M − R W. All three signal-system solves (signal, A^H noise weights, covariances) reuse these factors through the same lax.custom_linear_solve wrapper. The matvec and derivative structure are unchanged; the trans 0/1/2 solves use A = [[P,0],[R,S]]·[[I,W],[0,I]]. Candidate 1 results are recorded in experiments/notes/claude-linear-algebra.md: first run 31.509 s vs 35.737 s baseline, warm 10.88 s, official checks pass, strict array check fails on 3 gradient entries (max relative 1.5e-6).

data.hypothesis: Restoring candidate 1's solver should reproduce its measurements: first run about 31.4–31.5 s, warm about 10.9 s, carrier, signal and powers bitwise identical to baseline, noise relative L2 about 2e-8, and the same 3 gradient entries failing strict comparison at relative ≤1.5e-6. That gives a repeat timing sample for the best linear-algebra configuration and leaves the branch head on it.
data.change_summary: Candidate 3 rejects candidate 2 (block/Schur factorization) and restores candidate 1's dense shared-LU solver as the branch head. One LU(A) per frequency serves the signal solve, the A^H noise-weight solve (via LU(A)^H) and the covariance solve. The only code difference from candidate 1 is that `_lu_solve` now also accepts matrix right-hand sides; the vector path is unchanged. Candidate 2 cut warm runtime by 1.34 s (9.53 vs 10.88 s), but forward and gradient compile time grew by about 1.1 s. Its first run was 31.24 s (full) and 32.14 s (screen), vs candidate 1's 31.51 s and 31.43 s, so there was no reliable gain. Its numerics were about 10–100× worse: signal relative L2 2.6e-6, noise 1.7e-6, gradient idx 161 relative 6.4e-6. Notes and handoff are in experiments/notes/claude-linear-algebra.md.

The forward computation is the same elementwise math on the same inputs, with an exactly remapped output selection. Prediction: forward and gradient compile decrease by about 0.1–0.5 s, depending on the share of constant rows, which is unknown. Execute is unchanged or slightly lower. stage_policy.screen: Complete physical workload, provisional checks; omits finite-difference gradient sanity check and strict saved-array comparison.
stage_policy.full: Official full benchmark plus separate strict saved-array / all-gradient comparison.
stage_policy.objective: Minimize complete first-run time, including imports/setup, compilation, execution and transfer.
stage_policy.pareto: Same-cohort valid full results only. Exact observed Pareto membership is separate from noise-qualified progress.
stage_policy.expansion: Coordinator freezes a new round after reviewed guidance; frozen per-lane stall_limit applies (default 3). No automatic budget extensions.

nodes.hypothesis: Candidates 1 and 2 match the forward outputs bit for bit, but their whole gradient differs from baseline at about 9e-10 relative L2, where the parent was at about 1e-17. So the difference comes from operations that only run in the reverse pass. My leading guess, unverified, is that with k=1 every inner batch dimension has size 1. XLA simplifies such dimensions away, which picks different dot and triangular-solve kernels for the reverse pass than the batched parent uses. With k=2 the batch dimension is real, which should bring back the parent's batched kernels and strict agreement on index 161. Blocks of two should keep most of the memory and cache benefit, at about 1% extra solve work from the padding. Expected: forward slightly above 9.0 s and RSS slightly above 7.3 GB.

Gradient index 161 (boundary01.power) failed with a value identical to candidate 1's to within about 1e-14. That rules out the carrier accumulation-order explanation.

nodes.hypothesis: Target phases: forward compile (6.47 s) and gradient compile (1.29 s) in job 57ef1df7 (3b80507). Mechanism: the slot masks are per group, so if any single row reads an optimized index in a slot, every row's input in that slot carries a tangent. Examples are surface reflectivity and tuning on non-optimized mirrors, and space length on non-optimized spaces. Splitting off the all-constant rows and gradient-stopping all their slots removes their residuals and transposes. The forward computation is the same elementwise math on the same inputs, with an exactly remapped output selection. Prediction: forward and gradient compile decrease by about 0.1–0.5 s, depending on the share of constant rows, which is unknown. Execute is unchanged or slightly lower. Forward outputs should be bitwise identical, assuming XLA kernels are per-element identical across batch sizes (unverified; strict rtol covers it). The gradient should be identical or within reordering. Reject on a strict failure or a total slower than 19.57 s beyond noise.
nodes.change_summary: Candidate 3 (3b80507, LOWER_SLOT_PRUNING) passed official and strict checks in full job 57ef1df7 and is kept as the new branch best. The first run took 19.567 s, against 19.766 s for 10a311f; forward compile dropped by 0.15 s and gradient compile by 0.03 s. Forward outputs were bitwise identical, and the gradient's max normalized error stayed at 1.6e-8. This is the lowest full-valid total observed in cohort 10567ad0 so far, but it is one observation and not yet confirmed. Candidate 4 adds row-level pruning. Each mixed component group is reordered on the host as [rows that read an optimized or linked index, all-constant rows], with parameter_indices and output_rows remapped to match. update() then evaluates the constant rows with every slot gradient-stopped, so they get no linearization. Only simulate.py changed; setting ROW_SPLIT_PRUNING=False restores 3b80507.

nodes.hypothesis: Doing both A-solves in one call guarantees a single LU(A) per frequency. That saves one n≈751 complex LU per frequency if XLA did not already merge the duplicate LU (not checked against HLO). It also replaces two custom_linear_solve and triangular-solve paths with one, in both the forward and reverse passes, so execution and compile time may drop. The gain is unmeasured and may be about zero if the LU was already merged. Numerically the factorization and pivots are the same. Only the multi-column triangular solves and the order in which A's cotangent terms are added change, at rounding level, much like frequency-batching candidate 7, which passed the strict check. The main risk is strict gradient index 161.

Target phase: build, 0.807 s (3.7% of the first run) in full job f60d64b6 for 745f5c3.

Mechanism: build() runs about 30 eager jnp scalar ops per mirror or beamsplitter and several per space edge. Each one adds dispatch cost, primitive first-use compilation and host conversions (np.array of JAX scalars). NumPy gives the same structure without JAX dispatch.

Why outputs should stay bitwise identical: from the source, every such off-diagonal base entry is overwritten at the identical (row, column) by the carrier update instructions:
- mirror: rows [1,1,3,3], columns [0,2,0,2];
- beamsplitter: rows [1,1,3,3,5,5,7,7], columns [2,4,0,6,0,6,2,4];
- space: both directed entries.
The signal update instructions overwrite them in both sidebands, so ulp-level differences between NumPy and XLA never reach a solve.

Predicted: only the build phase drops. The ceiling is 0.81 s; the realistic saving is probably ≤0.3 s and unmeasured. Every other phase should be unchanged.

nodes.hypothesis: Target phases: forward compile (7.62 s) and gradient compile (1.96 s) in job 35abe628 (aa2b1ab). Candidate 1 (job 01ae3245) attributed about 2.9 s of that compile to the assembly linearization. Mechanism: the expanded parameter row carries a dense tangent, so the vjp forms derivative residuals and transposes for every component input. Many of those inputs never depend on a design variable; for example, 5 of the 7 surface inputs are constants. Gradient-stopping the slots that are provably constant gives them symbolic-zero tangents, so their residuals and transposes are never generated. Their true derivative is exactly zero, and stop_gradient is the identity in the forward pass. Prediction: forward and gradient compile both go down, and lower times go down slightly; the size is unknown and the ceiling is well under 2.9 s. Execute times stay the same or drop slightly. Forward outputs should be bitwise identical, and the gradient identical or within reordering (the dropped terms were exact 0*x contributions). Any forward difference or a strict failure rejects the candidate.

feedback-e0e48493fd77f39a5a23b4ee3a6a127.hypothesis: Target phases: gradient compile (2.42 s) and gradient lower (0.22 s) in job afea41cd. Mechanism: "direct_implicit" solves A^H with lax.custom_linear_solve, and its transpose rule adds a matvec transpose and a transpose_solve to the reverse program. "direct" uses jnp.linalg.solve on the explicit A^H, the original validated path. Prediction: gradient compile and lower decrease, by an unknown amount. Forward execute and memory may rise, because the transposed copy becomes an AD residual again. The net effect on first-run time is unknown. The forward pass factors the same matrix with the same pivots, so noise outputs should be identical or near-identical, and the gradient within reordering. Reject on a strict failure or a total slower than 17.85 s beyond noise.
feedback-e0e48493fd77f39a5a23b4ee3a6a127.change_summary: Candidate 5 (aac9904, COMPONENT_VALUE_REMAT, a combination of the narrow component-value checkpoint from 7d1ccc5 with my pruned branch) passed official and strict checks in full job afea41cd. The first run took 17.850 s against 19.543 s for parent 633689f, a gain of 1.69 s. Forward compile dropped by 2.92 s and gradient compile rose by 1.12 s, so the transfer was not one-for-one as it was for candidate 1. Forward outputs were bitwise identical and the gradient's max normalized error stayed at 1.6e-8. Warm runtime got worse by about 0.45 s (warm median 10.53 s vs 10.07 s); that is separate from the first-run objective. Candidate 5 is kept as the branch best. Candidate 6 is a one-flag test: NOISE_FACTOR_REUSE goes from "direct_implicit" to "direct", the setting 7d1ccc5 also uses.

feedback-e29d061dc2d56c886a2a87d56c441c4.hypothesis: Laser power affects the loop only through the carrier, which candidate 1 captured as a constant shared by all iterations. In the reverse pass, the scan added that constant's cotangents one frequency at a time across 101 iterations. The original vmap summed them in a single reduction, so the rounding differed slightly. Feeding the broadcast carrier entries and selections in as per-frequency inputs should restore the original order: per-frequency cotangents are stacked, summed by one reduction, then passed back through the gather. That should bring index 161 back within strict tolerance. Candidate 1's forward, gradient and memory gains should remain, apart from a few small extra broadcasts. Bitwise equality of the XLA reduction is not guaranteed.
feedback-e29d061dc2d56c886a2a87d56c441c4.change_summary: Candidate 2 keeps candidate 1's one-frequency-at-a-time loop (k=1) and changes how the frequency-shared inputs that depend on the parameters enter the loop. The gathered carrier connector entries and the detector carrier selections are now broadcast to all 101 rows before the loop and passed in as per-frequency inputs, instead of being captured as constants shared by every iteration. Candidate 1 (aa4d230f) passed the official check and failed strict. Its full run took 22.076 s versus 24.657 s for the parent. Forward execution took 9.12 s (parent 11.51), gradient execution 0.68 s (1.81), warm median 10.07 s (13.80), and peak RSS 7.27 GB (12.55). All physical outputs matched exactly. One gradient entry failed strict: index 161, boundary01.power, with relative error 1.9e-7 against rtol 1e-7. Nothing was run locally for candidate 2.

feedback-e50b01fdfb759cdcdf8b5a30fafd383.hypothesis: Candidate 4 placed the strict drift in the solve path when it runs inside the scan. Comparing it with candidate 2 suggested that about 1.1 s of the reverse-pass saving, and much of the RSS saving, came from running assembly per frequency. With assembly in the loop and the solves batched, strict should pass and part of candidate 1's gain should come back. My guess is gradient execution around 0.7–1.0 s and first run between 22 and 24.7 s; that is unmeasured. Risks: the stacked assembly outputs bring back about 1.8 GB of materialized matrices. Also, component-function gradients compiled inside the scan could still round differently, which would show up as a different strict failure pattern.
feedback-e50b01fdfb759cdcdf8b5a30fafd383.change_summary: Candidate 6 adds a third loop scope, "assemble", and sets k=1 with that scope. The loop now covers matrix assembly only: signal component updates, carrier connector scaling, conjugation and noise-matrix update, run per frequency. The stacked matrices then go into the unchanged full-vmap solve and noise section. Candidate 5 (7e00e16b, default None) is validated. It passed official and strict, physical outputs were exact, and the gradient's maximum absolute error was 4.547e-13, the same as the parent's. First run was 24.815 s (parent 24.657), warm median 14.08 s, RSS 12.55 GB. That confirms the refactor and the operator's default are strict-safe, and that the drift in candidates 1–4 comes from running solves inside the loop. Nothing was run locally.

feedback-eb3130b8290944dc70b88eaf492fe10.hypothesis:
Target phase: forward execute, 8.609 s (38.5% of the 22.366 s first run), full job ab12c14c29354bad9aa6dc024c91f8e6 on seed 96474bd. Gradient execute (1.475 s) is a secondary target.

Mechanism: the parent's "broadcast" mode builds a (101,751,751) complex broadcast of the noise matrix, about 0.9 GB, for the batched einsum. It is probably kept as an AD residual, and its cotangent becomes a dense (101,751,751) outer-product reduction. Earlier, the single-run pair noise-reuse c1 (f3139c7) to c2 (e525ee5) removed that broadcast with a GEMM and measured −0.9 GB RSS, forward −0.35 s, gradient −0.22 s and total −0.76 s. That GEMM changed rounding (gradient margin 0.949). rowmap instead performs, for each row, the same (751x751)x(751xD) product as the batched dot, without the broadcast.

Prediction: lower peak RSS (up to about 0.9 GB) and slightly lower forward and gradient execute. The upper bound is about 0.76 s; that is an opportunity bound, not an expected result. Possible costs are loop overhead and slightly higher compile time.
feedback-eb3130b8290944dc70b88eaf492fe10.change_summary: Candidate 1 adds NOISE_REUSE_MODE="rowmap" and makes it the default in differometor/simulate.py. The single shared 751x751 noise matrix is contracted row by row inside lax.map (einsum "ij,dj->di" for each signal row). Before, it was broadcast to (101,751,751) for the batched einsum. LU usage is unchanged: A is factored once for the signal and covariance solves, and A^H is factored separately. Notes are in experiments/notes/claude-profile-guided-v1.md. Nothing was run locally.

feedback-f188b6777904d6920f17b1b695a7f10.hypothesis: Target phases: forward compile (6.62 s) and gradient compile (1.32 s) in job 3a030c65 (10a311f). Mechanism: space_lower, space_modulation_lower and laser_frequency_modulation_lower rebuild their inputs with jnp.array before calling the base function. The rebuild turns candidate 2's symbolic-zero tangents for constant slots (frequency, refractive index) back into dense tangents, so the vjp still forms their derivative residuals and transposes. Calling the base function directly on separate scalars, with slot 0 negated, keeps the zeros symbolic. Exactness: the same scalars reach the same base function, so forward outputs should be bitwise identical and the gradient identical or within reordering. Prediction: forward and gradient compile both decrease slightly, likely ≤0.3 s combined; execute is unchanged. Reject on any forward difference, a strict failure, or a total slower than 19.77 s beyond noise.
feedback-f188b6777904d6920f17b1b695a7f10.change_summary: Candidate 2 (10a311f, COMPONENT_SLOT_PRUNING) passed official and strict checks in full job 3a030c65 and is kept as the new branch best. The first run took 19.766 s, against 21.550 s for parent aa2b1ab (job 35abe628). Forward compile dropped by 1.00 s (7.62 to 6.62), gradient compile by 0.64 s (1.96 to 1.32), and both lower phases by about 0.05 s each; execute times were unchanged. Forward outputs were bitwise identical, and the gradient's max normalized error was 1.6e-8, the same as the parent. Candidate 3 extends the pruning to the *_lower component variants. These rebuilt a dense parameter vector with jnp.array([-p0, p1, p2]), which brought back dense tangents. They now call the base function directly through _ParameterSlots with slot 0 negated, so the values are identical. Only simulate.py changed; setting LOWER_SLOT_PRUNING=False restores 10a311f.

concepts.title: Build static setup arrays on the host
concepts.before: Small setup operations used JAX array construction and eager kernels.
concepts.after: NumPy builds concrete setup values and index arrays before conversion to JAX, reducing setup dispatch and compilation.
concepts.attribution: Source mechanism; no isolated per-line timing measurement.

concepts.title: Specialize component evaluation by type
concepts.before: A batched dynamic switch selected each component function.
concepts.after: Group rows by their known component function and preserve an output permutation. Each group evaluates only its own function.
concepts.attribution: Source mechanism; no isolated per-line timing measurement.

concepts.title: Remove derivatives of constant inputs
concepts.before: Dense component input vectors carried tangent entries even for constant slots.
concepts.after: Static masks identify optimized or linked inputs. Separate scalar slots and stop_gradient remove derivative terms whose true derivatives are zero; lower-sideband variants preserve these scalar slots.
concepts.attribution: Source mechanism; no isolated per-line timing measurement.

concepts.title: Split constant rows from differentiable rows
concepts.before: A group-level active slot made the same slot active for every row.
concepts.after: Stable row partitions evaluate fully constant rows with all tangents stopped, then restore the original output order. The recorded parent trial was within timing noise.
concepts.attribution: Source mechanism; no isolated per-line timing measurement.

concepts.title: Checkpoint only component arithmetic
concepts.before: Saving component linearization residuals enlarged the forward program; checkpointing the whole assembly shifted work to backward compilation.
concepts.after: Recompute component values during reverse mode while retaining integer indexing results. Dense scatter and solves stay outside this checkpoint.
concepts.attribution: Source mechanism; no isolated per-line timing measurement.

concepts.title: Bound assembly by frequency
concepts.before: All frequency rows were assembled as one large vectorized program.
concepts.after: Use one-row assembly chunks while retaining full-vectorized solves. All 101 frequencies are still evaluated.
concepts.attribution: Source mechanism; no isolated per-line timing measurement.

concepts.title: Reuse invariant noise assembly and signal factors
concepts.before: Repeated rows assembled identical noise matrices and signal solves could refactor the same coefficient matrix.
concepts.after: A builder proof enables noise-row reuse; the direct_implicit path shares the signal LU and keeps an explicit conjugate-transposed noise solve.
concepts.attribution: Source mechanism; no isolated per-line timing measurement.

candidates.summary: Fast host/sparse approach with strict numerical mismatches and additional gradient findings. Review the exact diagnostics before selecting it.

concepts.title: Build static setup arrays on the host
concepts.before: Small setup operations used JAX array construction and eager kernels.
concepts.after: NumPy builds concrete setup values and index arrays before conversion to JAX, reducing setup dispatch and compilation.
concepts.attribution: Source mechanism; no isolated per-line timing measurement.

concepts.title: Specialize component evaluation by type
concepts.before: A batched dynamic switch selected each component function.
concepts.after: Group rows by their known component function and preserve an output permutation. Each group evaluates only its own function.
concepts.attribution: Source mechanism; no isolated per-line timing measurement.

concepts.title: Remove derivatives of constant inputs
concepts.before: Dense component input vectors carried tangent entries even for constant slots.
concepts.after: Static masks identify optimized or linked inputs. Separate scalar slots and stop_gradient remove derivative terms whose true derivatives are zero; lower-sideband variants preserve these scalar slots.
concepts.attribution: Source mechanism; no isolated per-line timing measurement.

concepts.title: Represent and solve structural sparsity
concepts.before: Dense matrices represented mostly unoccupied optical-system entries.
concepts.after: Build structural CSC patterns and solve with SciPy SuperLU through callbacks. Strict numerical differences must be assessed separately from official checks.
concepts.attribution: Source mechanism; no isolated per-line timing measurement.

concepts.title: Evaluate component arithmetic on the host
concepts.before: XLA compiled the component bodies and their derivatives.
concepts.after: NumPy component evaluation and a custom JVP move this arithmetic to the host.
concepts.attribution: Source mechanism; no isolated per-line timing measurement.

concepts.title: Fuse the optical pass behind a custom reverse derivative
concepts.before: Carrier, signal and noise operations were traced as a large JAX computation.
concepts.after: A host plan evaluates the forward pass with an explicit reverse pass behind a custom VJP. Broader transformation support and diagnostic failures remain separate evidence.
concepts.attribution: Source mechanism; no isolated per-line timing measurement.

concepts.title: Reduce compiler optimization for small residual programs
concepts.before: Default XLA optimization was applied to the remaining small callback/readout programs.
concepts.after: Package defaults request optimization level 0 and disable CPU fusion emitters before backend initialization, respecting existing flags. This process-wide setting is visible in the source diff.
concepts.attribution: Source mechanism; no isolated per-line timing measurement.

concepts.title: Build static setup arrays on the host
concepts.before: Small setup operations used JAX array construction and eager kernels.
concepts.after: NumPy builds concrete setup values and index arrays before conversion to JAX, reducing setup dispatch and compilation.
concepts.attribution: Source mechanism; no isolated per-line timing measurement.

concepts.title: Specialize component evaluation by type
concepts.before: A batched dynamic switch selected each component function.
concepts.after: Group rows by their known component function and preserve an output permutation. Each group evaluates only its own function.
concepts.attribution: Source mechanism; no isolated per-line timing measurement.

concepts.title: Remove derivatives of constant inputs
concepts.before: Dense component input vectors carried tangent entries even for constant slots.
concepts.after: Static masks identify optimized or linked inputs. Separate scalar slots and stop_gradient remove derivative terms whose true derivatives are zero; lower-sideband variants preserve these scalar slots.
concepts.attribution: Source mechanism; no isolated per-line timing measurement.

concepts.title: Represent and solve structural sparsity
concepts.before: Dense matrices represented mostly unoccupied optical-system entries.
concepts.after: Build structural CSC patterns and solve with SciPy SuperLU through callbacks. Strict numerical differences must be assessed separately from official checks.
concepts.attribution: Source mechanism; no isolated per-line timing measurement.

concepts.title: Evaluate component arithmetic on the host
concepts.before: XLA compiled the component bodies and their derivatives.
concepts.after: NumPy component evaluation and a custom JVP move this arithmetic to the host.
concepts.attribution: Source mechanism; no isolated per-line timing measurement.

concepts.title: Fuse the optical pass behind a custom reverse derivative
concepts.before: Carrier, signal and noise operations were traced as a large JAX computation.
concepts.after: A host plan evaluates the forward pass with an explicit reverse pass behind a custom VJP. Broader transformation support and diagnostic failures remain separate evidence.
concepts.attribution: Source mechanism; no isolated per-line timing measurement.
